How to choose tyre pressure for city riding

26

By Lea Hartmann · 3 March 2026

27 28

The number printed on the tyre sidewall is a maximum, not a recommendation. On cobbles and patched asphalt, most riders are faster and more comfortable a good way below it.

29 30

Start from the tyre width

31 32

As a starting point for a rider of about 75 kg: 28 mm tyres at 5 to 5.5 bar, 35 mm tyres at 3.5 to 4 bar, and 47 mm tyres at 2.5 to 3 bar. Put about 0.3 bar less in the front than in the rear.

33 34

Then adjust by feel

35

If the bike bounces over cobbles, let some air out. If the tyre squirms in corners or you feel the rim hit an edge, add some. Check the pressure every two weeks: tyres lose air slowly even without a puncture.

Winter chain care: keep your drivetrain running through the salt season

26

By Jonas Albrecht · 18 November 2025 · Print version

27 28

Every January we replace more chains than in the rest of the year together. Road salt and wet grit turn a chain into sandpaper, and a worn chain then wears out the cassette and chainrings as well. Ten minutes a week keeps most of that away.

29 30

Clean it, do not drown it

31 32

Wipe the chain with a dry rag while you turn the cranks backwards. If it is very dirty, use a little degreaser on the rag, not a jet of water: a pressure washer pushes water past the seals into the bearings.

33 34

Use a wet lube or wax, and wipe off the extra

35 36

In winter a wet lube lasts longer between rain rides. Put one drop on each roller, turn the cranks for a minute, and then wipe the outside of the chain. Lube that stays on the outside only collects dirt.

37 38

Measure wear once a month

39

A chain checker costs a few euros. When it shows 0.5 % wear on an 11- or 12-speed chain, or 0.75 % on a chain with fewer gears, change the chain before it damages the cassette.

40 41

If you would rather leave it to us, the chain is checked and cleaned in every service – see our repair prices.

content.text: Here's what I found, roughly by severity: 1. **`robots.txt` blocks all of `/blog/`** — but the blog has two finished, dated articles that are linked from the homepage and listed in `sitemap.xml`. This alone would keep your best long-form content out of Google entirely. 2. **The "Shop" nav link isn't a real link** — every page uses `Shop` instead of ``. Crawlers don't reliably follow that, so `/shop/` has no crawlable internal links pointing to it. 3. **`services.html` (English prices page) has ``**, while the German equivalent `de/leistungen.html` does not. Your core English commercial page is hidden from Google — likely why English is worse than German. 4. **Broken links to a page that doesn't exist**: `/repairs.html` is referenced in `sitemap.xml`, in the blog article, and on the shop product page — but the real page is `services.html`. 5. **Duplicate `` and meta description across all 3 blog pages** (`Blog | Werkbank Cycles`) — the index and both articles share identical titles/descriptions, which hurts click-through and reads as duplicate content to Google. 6. `hreflang="ge"` typo (should be `de`) on `contact.html` and `de/kontakt.html`, breaking the English↔German page pairing. 7. `de/leistungen.html` is missing its reciprocal `hreflang="en"` back to `services.html`. 8. `shop/tubeless-kit.html` has two conflicting `<link rel="canonical">` tags (one pointing at `/shop/`, one at itself). 9. `blog/tyre-pressure.html`'s canonical URL uses `http://` instead of `https://`. 10. No structured data (LocalBusiness) — a quick win for local search/Maps visibility, using facts already on the page. I'll fix all of these now, starting with the highest-impact ones.

All three EN/DE page pairs (home, contact/kontakt, services/leistungen) now correctly reference each other with valid `de`/`en` codes and reciprocal links. That covers everything I found. Here's the summary.

## What I fixed

**Blocking indexing outright**
- `robots.txt` had `Disallow: /blog/` — blocking your two finished, dated blog articles from Google entirely, even though they're linked from the homepage and in the sitemap. Removed.
- `services.html` (English prices page) had `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` — hiding your English pricing page from Google while the German version wasn't hidden. Removed.
- **`de/index.html`'s canonical tag pointed to the English homepage** instead of itself — telling Google "index the English page instead of this one." This alone could explain most of your German-visibility problem. Fixed to self-reference `/de/`.

**Crawlability**
- The "Shop" nav link was a `<span onclick="location.href=...">`, not a real `<a href>`, on all 12 pages — search engines don't reliably follow that, so `/shop/` had no crawlable internal links. Replaced with real anchors everywhere.
- Two internal links pointed to `/repairs.html`, which doesn't exist (real page is `/services.html`) — in the blog article and the shop product page.
- `sitemap.xml` also listed the nonexistent `/repairs.html`, and listed `/thanks.html` (a noindex form-confirmation page that shouldn't be submitted for indexing). Both removed.

**Duplicate/incorrect metadata**
- All three blog pages (`/blog/`, the two articles) shared the identical `<title>` and meta description. Gave each article its own, matching its actual content.
- `hreflang="ge"` (invalid code) on `contact.html` and `de/kontakt.html` → fixed to `de`.
- `de/leistungen.html` was missing its reciprocal `hreflang="en"` back to `services.html`.
- `shop/tubeless-kit.html` had two conflicting canonical tags (one pointing at `/shop/`, one at itself). Removed the wrong one.
- `blog/tyre-pressure.html`'s canonical used `http://` instead of `https://`.

**Added**
- `BicycleStore` JSON-LD structured data on both homepages (name, address, phone, hours) — all facts already visible on the page — to support local/Maps search.

## Verified
Re-read every edited file, confirmed no leftover `onclick`, `/repairs.html`, or `hreflang="ge"` references, checked all 12 sitemap URLs resolve to real files, and re-checked every canonical/hreflang pair site-wide for self-consistency.

## Left as proposals (need your call, not code fixes)
- **German content depth**: the blog only exists in English. Translating the two existing articles into German would give you German-language long-tail content — I can do this if you want, but it's a real content task, not a quick fix, so I didn't do it unprompted.
- **Server-level checks I can't verify from these files alone**: whether `http://` actually redirects to `https://`, and www vs non-www canonicalization — that's hosting/DNS config outside this repo.
- Two shop items ("Chain wax", "Resin brake pads") have no product page of their own, so they can't rank for their own searches — worth a page each if you want that traffic.
